churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, formatting and config are well isolated behind a few lib modules, so most requirement changes touch few files. But the framework's type-safety is systematically erased with `as any`/`any`, no tsconfig means none of it is checked, and one undocumented internal sentinel is copy-pasted across five handlers — exactly the code that breaks silently on the next 0.x bump of a pre-1.0 framework.

findings.issue: Every route casts `context.props.GET as any` and types all API payloads as `any`, defeating Gracile's typed handler→template props pipeline and hiding API shape drift until runtime.
findings.suggestion: Type the handler return values explicitly and let defineRoute propagate them into `context.props.GET` (as its typings are designed to do); replace `any` with minimal interfaces for the PokeAPI resources.

findings.issue: Reliance on the undocumented internal `gracile-static` hostname sentinel (duplicated in pokemon/[name].ts:104, moves/[name].ts:28, abilities/[name].ts:19, types/[name].ts:24) — it exists in engine's render.ts but is not in any docs and could change in a 0.x release.
findings.suggestion: Centralize the check in one exported helper in lib/ (e.g. `isBuildStub(url)`) with a comment citing the engine source, so a framework change is a one-file fix.

findings.issue: No tsconfig.json and no devDependencies: the TypeScript sources are transpile-only (Vite strips types), so nothing ever type-checks the `any`-heavy boundary code.
findings.suggestion: Add Gracile's shipped tsconfig (`@gracile/gracile/tsconfigs/*`) plus a `typecheck` script to package.json.

findings.issue: This single route's handler lacks the build-time stub guard that the home route has, so it performs a live API fetch during `vite build` (harmless today only because its output isn't prerendered, but inconsistent and fragile).
findings.suggestion: Apply the same stub guard (ideally the shared helper from finding 2).

findings.issue: Server-side fetches have no timeout or AbortController, so a hung upstream request stalls a page render indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Pass `AbortSignal.timeout(n)` to fetch and let ApiError distinguish 504-style timeouts.

findings.issue: URL handling by `startsWith`/`slice` string surgery (api.ts:83-88) and id extraction by regex (api.ts:95-99) instead of the URL API — brittle against unusual URL forms.
findings.suggestion: Parse with `new URL(...)` and read `.pathname` for prefix/id checks.

findings.issue: The try/catch → `responseInit.status = 404` → `notFound` pattern is copy-pasted across four route handlers.
findings.suggestion: Extract a `notFound()` helper that sets status and returns the shared props shape.

findings.issue: `@import url('./tokens.css')` adds a serial extra request for static assets served from /public, outside Gracile's Vite CSS pipeline.
findings.suggestion: Link both stylesheets, or move styles into the build pipeline (sibling `.css` route assets / Vite CSS imports) so they're bundled and hashed.

findings.issue: Dead import: `orMissing` is imported but unused in this file.
findings.suggestion: Remove it (a lint step would catch this).

summary: This is current-generation Gracile throughout: the 0.11 route API, document/template split, client-script convention and Express adapter all match the official docs and starter exactly, on a lean four-dependency stack at latest majors. The forward-looking weak spot is typing and internal coupling — `as any` at every handler→template boundary, no tsconfig so nothing checks it, and an undocumented build-time sentinel (`gracile-static`) pasted into five handlers. Data access is otherwise nicely centralized in `lib/`, so fixing the type boundaries and centralizing the stub guard would make upgrades low-friction.

apis.replacement: No public API exists; verified against engine source (packages/engine/src/routes/render.ts) — treat as internal and isolate in one helper
